messages:
maya: quick sync 10min1 1 - onboarding morpheus13b int4 on A10G. canary started and were seeing intermittent OOMs when several long requests overlap (~1.2k-2k gen). logs show slab stripe oscillation and eviction storms. short repro attached.

rafi: can you paste the exact config and a minimal log snippet? curious whether this is the classic prefetch wave issue or something new.

maya: runtime 2.3.1, kernel=optimized-attn-v2, config used for canary:
```
quant: int4
prefetch: true
batch_size: 14
max_new_tokens: 1800
kv_reserve: 0.12
runtime.flags:
  enable_async_compact: false
  staggered_prefetch: false
```
log:
```
[2026-03-23T07:41:02Z] slab stripe expand 64->192MB
[2026-03-23T07:41:03Z] kv_prefetch miss burst 78%
[2026-03-23T07:41:03Z] GPU alloc fail 56MB -> OOM
[2026-03-23T07:41:03Z] eviction loop start, compaction deferred
```

sasha: ok. pattern looks like multiple requests trigger simultaneous prefetch waves which push slab allocations past the slow compactor cadence. two levers: increase kv_reserve and smooth prefetch timing (stagger).

jamie: I've got a prototype runtime flag that staggers prefetch start times across batched requests to avoid synchronized waves. it delays prefetch by an offset derived from request start hash mod micro-window. low-risk to test on canary.

rafi: interesting. propose immediate mitigations:
- lower max_new_tokens default for canary to 1200
- reduce batch_size to 8 for int4 morpheus
- raise kv_reserve to 0.22
- enable staggered_prefetch=true (experimental) and enable_async_compact=true

maya: applied locally and repro runs went from ~40 OOMs/1000 to 0 OOMs/1000. latency p95 increased ~6% but stable. config used:
```
max_new_tokens: 1200
batch_size: 8
kv_reserve: 0.22
runtime.flags:
  staggered_prefetch: true
  enable_async_compact: true
```

sasha: nice. add CI smoke: 25 long-turn traces under concurrency 4, assert 0 OOMs and p95 <= baseline*1.2. ci-bot?

ci-bot: created job morpheus-staggered-prefetch-smoke. thresholds: 0 OOMs, p95 <= baseline*1.20.

rafi: separate concern: nightly quality eval shows a small drop on list/enumeration tasks when int4 + staggered prefetch + smaller batch is used. we need an A/B to isolate cause (quant vs scheduling vs batch-size).

jamie: scheduled A/B:
- A: master int8 baseline
- B1: int4 + staggered_prefetch + batch_size 8
- B2: int4 + no-stagger + batch_size 8
- B3: int4 + staggered + batch_size 12
collect token-level diffs and n-gram mismatch metrics.

sasha: also run a quick quant-recalibration sweep (per-channel scale tweak) overnight. if B2 matches B1 then it's scheduling, otherwise quant.

maya: ops: rolling the canary defaults change to canary cohort (5% traffic) with staggered_prefetch=true and kv_reserve=0.22. PR: https://internal/pr/4391. monitoring dashboards added: slab-stripe-by-node, kv-miss-heatmap, staggered-offset-distribution.

ops-bot: alert rule morpheus-slab-churn created. will page if slab stripe growth >150MB within 2m on >3 nodes.

rafi: fallback plan: if nightly eval shows token-acc delta >3% on eval suite, route long-trace (estimated token >800) requests to int8 variant or to kernel fallback (optimized-attn-v1) which has more conservative prefetch.

jamie: follow-ups: (1) open eng-runtime ticket to make staggered_prefetch default-safe with tunable window, (2) land async compaction improvements to reduce slab tail latency, (3) publish canary postmortem + perf sheets.

sasha: I'll run the A/B and quant recal overnight and post results here tomorrow. thanks team. :rocket:

maya: monitoring 1h in: KV miss rate down 35%, slab spikes reduced, no new OOMs. p95 +6%. keeping canary at 5% until CI smoke and nightly A/B clear. closing thread for now. will reopen if alerts fire.
